records.reason: Measure m30 at 20/1 and 100 ul between measured 10/1 (2420964caf34a1de2a5d) and 50/1 (605436d35600502e8c2e). Together with the selected m35 condition, this tests the predicted reversal in intermediate-ratio finish ordering between the two para-halogenated acetophenones.

Measure m35 at 20/1 and 100 ul. Its measured V2 is below m30 at both 5/1 and 50/1 (8200df9dd2dce17ed7d1, a31d24ee8162e1eca101), yet the model predicts a later intermediate finish. The matched m30/m35 pair directly tests this curvature.

Measure ortho-methoxyacetophenone m127 at 5/1 and 50 ul. Its predicted onset is later than the measured 10/1 onset in 4b408fbbcfc4c054f284. This point starts a fixed-loading 5/1, 20/1, 50/1 experiment to distinguish real local behavior from unstable onset interpolation.

Measure m127 at 20/1 and 50 ul, between measured 10/1 (4b408fbbcfc4c054f284) and the selected 50/1 point. This locates onset growth and finish growth separately in a sparsely anchored methoxy-ketone response curve.

Complete the m127 fixed-50-ul experiment at 50/1. The predicted 37.4/72.9 mL response is a substantial extrapolation from measured 10/1 at 6.6/21.4 mL (4b408fbbcfc4c054f284); the intermediate selections make this label informative about transition shape.

Measure para-methoxyacetophenone m115 at 10/1 and 100 ul. The latest 0/1 measurement had a substantial acquisition-time V2 underestimate (368ea7ae793fdfdcf602), while measured 2/1 already finishes near 19.9 mL (f2931e18ce0362f7a6c0). This extends endpoint calibration and tests transfer against the selected ortho isomer.

Measure sulfur-ketone m128 at 5/1 and 150 ul. The latest 100-ul measurement was 20.6/36.9 mL and substantially later than its acquisition prediction (892c3900698d3de38b1c). This loading contrast tests whether the repaired response transfers across sample amount before extrapolating from the measured 10/1 condition.

Measure sulfur-aldehyde m129 at 2/1 and 100 ul. Measured 0/1 and 5/1 were relatively compact despite large historical overpredictions (c18c041c752aba7ff0e4, cf8ab33c25ad391a584c). This anchors the strong-eluent region where the current predicted finish already exceeds the measured 5/1 finish.

Measure m129 at 10/1 and 100 ul, completing a loading-controlled bridge between measured 5/1 (cf8ab33c25ad391a584c) and 50/1 (d54c93a11164b4abac6e). Paired with selected 2/1, it tests where sulfur-aldehyde retention actually begins to increase.

Measure diphenyl sulfoxide m199 at 5/1 and 150 ul. Measured 5/1 at 100 ul is 28.5/52.3 mL (714004602e6452764d9a), whereas 2/1 at 150 ul is 12.1/22.7 mL (d49f2ae16cf70d54ccf4). This supplies the loading control needed to interpret the selected 10/1 point.

Measure m199 at 10/1 and 150 ul. The model predicts almost no finish increase from the selected 5/1 condition, despite the large measured 2/1-to-5/1 increase. The matched pair discriminates a genuine plateau from underestimated weak-eluent sensitivity.

Measure methoxybenzoate m87 at 10/1 and 50 ul. Measured 1/1 and 2/1 at this loading are compact (fd3a369b0bc0681cddd7, a05ccef9e073f648892e). This gives a lower-ratio anchor for the selected 50/1 experiment and tests transfer of methoxy-substituted aromatic ester responses.

Measure m87 at 50/1 and 50 ul, matched to selected 10/1. Its large predicted retention and very high CW distance indicate an extrapolated response region. Measured 20/1 at 150 ul (6d54149d618f026681ef) provides an additional, explicitly loading-shifted reference.

Measure benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester m78 at 50/1 and 150 ul. Existing 5/1 and 20/1 measurements at the same loading (6000105cb6734cff8146, c65ac14ffed8749381c1) make this a controlled test of continued weak-eluent growth and transfer across beta-ketoester environments.

Measure naphthylacetate m98 at 50/1 and 150 ul. The pool's highest CW distance accompanies an unmeasured high-ratio region, with measured 20/1 at 50 ul (3cd0aa35793392d15513) and 10/1 at 100 ul (b3f456e3c4a350277eaa) as loading-shifted anchors. This tests whether its ester environment develops the predicted late response.

Measure bromobenzofuran m8 at 50/1 and 150 ul. Measured 20/1 at the same loading remains at 4.8/16.6 mL (5806c857509e09634010), while the model predicts substantial further growth. The compact recent methoxynaphthalene result (3032c273eee09a2644c3) makes this a useful test of transfer between fused oxygen-containing aromatic environments.

Measure bromomalonate m74 at 50/1 and 100 ul beyond its measured 10/1 anchor (12ee64241e59d6b88e7a). Unsubstituted malonate m80 remained compact at 50/1 (f7d57d8bb988f7016502), so this label tests a specific substitution-dependent response rather than a generic multi-ester tail.

Measure pyridyl ketone m66 at 1/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 2/1 and 5/1 responses are already 19.0/55.1 and 47.4/119.3 mL (4659b6752f23c0b85f08, 49201b5817f204116f7f). This locates the lower-ratio onset of finish expansion in a basic heteroaromatic carbonyl family.

Measure cyclopropyl beta-ketoester m94 at 1/1 and 100 ul. Measured 0/1 at 150 ul is compact (d7457b516ddba0143275), and 5/1 at 100 ul finishes near 26.0 mL (a1809a6c4c3ada20bcb0). Together with selected 2/1, this tests the model's nearly flat low-ratio onset and finish predictions.

Measure m94 at 2/1 and 100 ul, matched to selected 1/1 and measured 5/1. The much later measured 20/1 response (e3a799d0fa90b649a157) makes the transition location consequential for transfer among beta-ketoesters.

Measure bromobenzyl alcohol m207 at 2/1 and 150 ul as the controlled lower-ratio member of a 2/1-to-5/1 pair. Existing 1/1 at 100 ul is compact (eb36ddda7c31d7efdac5), while the measured 5/1 loading contrast is unusually large.

Measure m207 at 5/1 and 150 ul. The 50-ul and 100-ul measurements differ sharply, at 21.2/34.0 versus 4.9/10.4 mL (4e5ead91320bd24d485e, ec6846c0fcb7df17c97d). This new loading level and the selected 2/1 control test whether a reproducible loading interaction explains the contrast.

Measure ethyl cinnamate m73 at 1/1 and 50 ul. Measured 1/1 at 100 ul is unusually late and narrow (2cf789c87f7c6325c020), and the 0/1 low-loading record has reversed endpoints (3d5a3094cb10eee37b37). This tests whether the late regime recurs at another loading without treating the anomalous records as a chemical rule.

Measure m73 at 0/1 and 150 ul, completing a loading sequence around conflicting low- and middle-loading behavior (3d5a3094cb10eee37b37, b187c8a6f7beb2c7f61f). This can constrain the ordinary predictive response and limit propagation of the isolated late low-loading record.

Measure naphthaldehyde m195 at 20/1 and 50 ul. Its 20/1, 150-ul record has slightly reversed endpoints and a late onset (a917c928912c74862968), while measured 50/1 onsets are earlier (7654254c03d9de79740f, 79362765eb92377a5970). Measure multifunctional ester m13 at 5/1 and 150 ul. This ID remains unmeasured in the supplied table. Its prediction closely inherits the measured 50-ul response (1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23); paired with selected 10/1, it tests whether that loading transfer is justified.

Measure m13 at 10/1 and 150 ul, matched to selected 5/1. The measured 50-ul curve rises from 23.9/40.1 to 53.0/93.3 mL (1cc3b837c6561b1c0a23, c4bb286978fe9078a303). This tests whether both endpoints preserve that steep ratio response at higher loading.

Measure aminoacetophenone m36 at 1/1 and 150 ul, directly preceding measured 2/1 at the same loading (9fcf89b00bb880c8a5ba). This anchors an uncovered strong-eluent condition for an amino-carbonyl scaffold and tests transfer against pyridyl ketones and amino esters.

Measure benzoylacetate m81 at 5/1 and 100 ul, before measured 10/1 and the conflicting 20/1 records (eb6c235e6ed90084bfc9, db2709229820b71e283b, 7e0c856a121512a6f891). This anchors finish behavior before the disputed regime and forms a matched loading pair.

Measure m81 at 5/1 and 150 ul, matched to selected 100 ul. The measured 10/1, 150-ul finish is much shorter than lower-loading finishes (7d402b3fad455f06fe68, ce11189a0e59d1798306). This tests whether that loading association is already present at 5/1 or remains condition-specific.

Measure terminal-methoxy aryl ketone m106 at 10/1 and 100 ul. Only its compact 0/1 condition is measured here (265b6eb5a10a34c937b1), leaving the predicted growing response poorly anchored. The selected 20/1 condition provides a fixed-loading slope experiment for this ether-carbonyl environment.

Measure m106 at 20/1 and 100 ul, matched to selected 10/1. High CW distance and predicted growth beyond the measured 0/1 anchor make this useful condition exploration. The pair tests how a remote ether changes retention response in a lipophilic aryl ketone.

hypotheses.content: Reducing the EA fraction can produce steep retention growth, but the transition and its magnitude depend strongly on scaffold. Carbonyl or acceptor counts alone do not justify a general late-retention correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels spanning transitions and compact controls can teach graph-condition interactions while preventing late-response families from shifting predictions for ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which weak-eluent responses transfer across methoxy esters, beta-ketoesters, bromomalonate, fused ethers, and basic carbonyl scaffolds?

hypotheses.content: Recorded sample loading and loading-plug conditions can affect V1 and V2 differently, but their response is scaffold-dependent and some apparent loading effects may include unexplained label variation. A single monotonic loading law remains unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched experiments test the nearly invariant loading predictions and identify whether endpoint-specific loading associations transfer between conditions. Sample volume and density-times-volume amount remain coupled in these contrasts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m81 and m207 reproduce their loading associations at adjacent ratios, and does the steep m13 ratio response persist at 150 ul?

hypotheses.content: Finish behavior needs endpoint-specific calibration: reasonably predicted onset can coexist with either substantial V2 overprediction or underprediction, including in strong-eluent conditions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Measuring both endpoints around response transitions can correct finish predictions without imposing a corresponding onset shift.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At low-ratio m94 and m66 conditions, does finish expansion precede, accompany, or lag onset growth?

hypotheses.content: Sulfur-containing ketones, aldehydes, and sulfoxides require local structure-condition calibration. Their historical errors have different signs, so correction learned for one sulfur environment may transfer poorly to another.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled sulfur-family experiments can distinguish functional-group placement, oxidation environment, solvent response, and loading associations instead of learning a shared sulfur offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m129 remain compact through 2/1 before rising at 10/1, and does m199 truly plateau between 5/1 and 10/1 at fixed loading?

hypotheses.content: Substitution-specific response curvature may explain the predicted intermediate ordering reversal between para-bromo and para-iodoacetophenone and the uncertain transfer between ortho- and para-methoxyacetophenone. These intermediate relationships remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These experiments discriminate nonseparable graph-solvent effects from interpolation artifacts among closely related aromatic ketones.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m30/m35 finish ordering actually cross at 20/1, and where does the m127 weak-eluent transition occur at fixed 50-ul loading?

hypotheses.content: Some labeled contrasts cannot be explained uniquely by the recorded inputs. Identical-condition labels can differ substantially, and a few records have V2 below V1. Measurement variation or absent metadata are possibilities, not established causes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Nearby measurements can constrain the predictive response and reduce spurious loading or solvent laws inferred from isolated inconsistent labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the unusual m73 and m195 regimes recur at adjacent loadings, or do new labels support a more ordinary local response?

feedback_interpretation: The latest acquisition outcomes strengthen local, endpoint-specific repair. m128 at 5/1 was substantially later than its acquisition prediction, while m205 at 2/1 and m72 at 1/1 were close enough to reduce the urgency of additional nearby measurements. Strong-eluent finish errors occurred in both directions: m115 was underpredicted, whereas m145 and m104 were overpredicted. The new m81 20/1 result conflicts with an earlier identical-input label, weakening any deterministic loading explanation for that region. Historical errors are used as acquisition-time evidence, not current-model residuals. I also corrected memory bookkeeping: dc73b789d0821495353b is m162 at 50/1, not m70 at 0/1; 0c5c35afb3a24375c153 is the sulfur-free m178; and 5d530b2f228ed39ff952 remains an unmeasured candidate.
batch_rationale: The batch emphasizes experiments that distinguish plausible response models. The matched m30/m35 conditions test an ordering reversal; the three-point m127 experiment locates curvature; sulfur-family pairs test whether recent repairs transfer across loading and chemical environment. m78, m87, m98, m8, m74, and m106 explore weak-eluent regions with limited direct anchoring, while low-ratio m94, m66, and m36 measurements constrain transition beginnings. Matched m13, m81, and m207 experiments test combined recorded loading responses and separate onset from finish behavior. The m73 and m195 selections address influential inconsistencies through adjacent conditions without assuming their causes. CW distance and single-model quantile spreads were secondary diagnostics; quantile crossing and nearly flat loading predictions limit their uncertainty interpretation. Sample amount and sample volume are coupled here, so the loading comparisons cannot establish independent causal effects. Together, these labels should improve generalization across Row conditions by teaching when structural analogies transfer, where solvent-response transitions occur, and which apparent relationships remain unstable under the supplied features.
